prompt:
사용자 요청 원문:
좋아. 이제 인스턴스를 다시 켜고 첫 태스크를 만들어보자.
필요한 CLI 인증부터 확인하고, 로봇 조립·데이터센터 정비 분야에서 산업 근거가 있고 기존 제출과 겹치지 않는 후보를 골라 제출 전 검토 단계까지 진행해줘.

확정된 제작 조건:
- Category: Impact on AI timelines. 로봇 조립 또는 데이터센터 정비 중 실제 산업에서 자동화할 의미가 있는 물리 조작 하나를 선택한다.
- 제조사 설치·정비 매뉴얼, 공식 조립 절차, 공개 설계, 실제 작업 영상·보고서의 원문으로 작업과 장비 형상·치수·절차를 입증한다. 추측이나 가상 산업 용도를 만들어내지 않는다.
- 여러 후보를 비교하고 목적·물리 기술·성공 조건의 신규성과 로봇의 어려운 조작 능력을 함께 검토하여 하나만 제작한다. 조작의 어려움은 극단적일 필요는 없지만 단순 물체 옮기기를 산업 이름만 바꾼 작업은 피한다.
- 모든 분야의 기존 accepted/pending/open 제출 및 우리 팀 기존 제출, 지정된 기존 벤치마크와 비교한다. 기하·색상·배치·시작 자세·난도만 다른 것은 새 태스크가 아니다. 선정 시점 및 완성 후 다시 전수 비교한다. 불확실한 중복을 통과시키지 않는다.
- 가능한 강체 PhysX 작업을 선택한다. 기존의 검증된 연성 에셋이 없다면 새 연성 솔버 연구는 하지 않는다. 실제 산업 장비의 형태와 중요한 물리 제약을 재현한다. 공개 에셋은 라이선스·출처·치수를 기록하고 적합하지 않으면 직접 제작한다.
- objective와 환경·부품 물리를 먼저 완성·진단한 뒤 YAM 전체 데모·채점기를 연결한다. 물체 순간이동/상태 덮어쓰기로 성공을 만들지 않는다. 관련 부품 파손·금지 동작·실패·부분 점수와 성공 유지 시간을 수치로 평가한다.
- 실제 simulator 측정·두 번의 full-score YAM 데모·실패/부분 점수 대조군·영상/원시 trace 및 깨끗한 경로 재현 검사를 수행한다. 미검증 수치와 성공을 만들어 보고하지 않는다.
- 모든 제작·검증을 마친 후에만 Dream 최종 평가 episode 1회. 실패나 불명 결과도 자동 재평가하지 않는다. 누적 $20 ledger를 준수하고 인증이 없으면 제작을 보존한 뒤 평가 대기한다.
- 결과는 이 run의 새로운 origin 브랜치에 보존한다. 원본 매뉴얼 전체/인증 정보는 공개하지 않는다. 50MB/file 또는 100MB checkpoint 초과는 먼저 보고한다.
- 완료 후 GPU를 stop하고 제출 전 검토 보고서·영상·채점 결과를 제공한다. 실제 미디어 업로드·대회 PR·승인은 하지 않는다.
- 기존 feature/close-snack-bag checkout 및 robocurve-snack-film 인스턴스는 별개 작업이므로 건드리지 않는다.

selected.title: Extract a 5378-series terminal with a single HT60630B blade
selected.objective: Hold the compatible housing with its locking tab upward, bend the wire down, insert one HT60630B blade beneath the locking tab, and pull the wire and tool together to remove the terminal.
skills: single-blade insertion beneath a recessed tab
coordinated same-direction tool and wire pull
selected.success_conditions: The selected 5378 terminal exits its cavity through robot-applied blade and pulling forces while the housing remains intact and no neighboring terminal is released. Zero for bypassing the locking tab, wire/crimp separation, housing damage, unintended extraction, or state overwrite. Exact force and damage thresholds remain blocked pending measurements.
selected.industrial_value: Molex provides an explicit manufacturer procedure for extracting individual 5378 terminals with this tool, establishing a real connector-service operation.
selected.dexterity: High. Unlike the selected dual-blade process, this sequence requires wire bending, insertion of one blade beneath a specific tab, and simultaneous withdrawal of the wire and tool.

evidence.quote: Individual terminals may be extracted from the housing using this tool.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 3, For 5378 Terminal Series

evidence.quote: Hold the housing with the locking tab facing up. Bend the wire down and insert one of the blades of the extraction tool into the housing under the locking tab.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 3, For 5378 Terminal Series, step 1

evidence.quote: Hold the wire against the extraction tool and gently pull the terminal by the wire and the extraction tool at the same time out from the housing in the direction shown.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 3, For 5378 Terminal Series, step 2

selected.asset_plan: Acquire the authoritative 5378 housing and terminal drawings and reference hardware before modeling. Use rigid PhysX geometry and an articulated locking tab calibrated from the actual parts. Validate wire-bending clearance, tab release, simultaneous pull, damage modes, and YAM reachability before full-demo work.
selected.risk: Not selected. It is meaningfully different in contact mechanics from the dual-blade 5556 procedure, but the acquired package lacks a 5378 housing drawing, selected part number, complete geometry, and robot-application evidence. It also shares the broader depinning objective, so it offers weaker novelty separation than the selected, better-specified four-circuit Mini-Fit Jr. setup.

comparisons.objective: Extract a spacer from a covered channel with a pusher, then recover and park both parts; candidate depins a retained electrical terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Axial pushing and subsequent pick-place versus recessed dual-blade tang depression maintained during an opposite-side wire pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Spacer must be pusher-extracted, nested, and tool parked; candidate requires only the selected terminal rear-extracted with housing, wire, and neighbors intact.
comparisons.reason: Both are tool-assisted extraction, but the retention-release mechanism, force sequence, and terminal-selectivity constraints are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Select a correctly fitting wrench, loosen a captive nut, and open a clamped arm; candidate removes a connector terminal by releasing internal tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Wrench-fit discrimination and rotary torque versus precision blade insertion, sustained tang depression, and coordinated axial pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Nut backed off without rounding and arm opened with a long hands-off hold; candidate requires selective terminal exit without housing, crimp, or neighbor damage.
comparisons.reason: The objectives and dominant manipulation mechanics differ beyond tool or geometry changes.

comparisons.objective: Remove a battery service plug before relocating busbars; candidate extracts one crimp terminal from inside a connector housing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grasp-and-pull of an unlatching gravity-held plug plus safe busbar transfer versus dual-blade internal release and simultaneous wire pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug out and busbars safely placed without hazardous ordering or bridging; candidate requires a particular terminal out while all adjacent terminals remain retained and undamaged.
comparisons.reason: The battery task does not model or require releasing internal retention tangs.

comparisons.objective: Release a spring-retained tool before pulling it free while keeping its fixture stable; candidate releases a spring-tang-retained terminal before pulling it free while preserving the housing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require overcoming spring retention and coordinating release with extraction; candidate adds recessed dual-blade alignment and opposite-side wire handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Both require the retained item fully clear, controlled, and the retaining fixture not displaced or damaged; candidate adds neighbor and crimp integrity.
comparisons.reason: The core objective, release-then-pull skill, and retained-fixture success state coincide; connector geometry and extra precision constraints do not by themselves establish novelty.

comparisons.objective: Latch a doll's harness tongues and chest clip; candidate unlatches and removes an internal electrical terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Strap placement and snap-latching versus tool-guided tang depression and sustained bimanual extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Harness components latched in safe positions without disturbing the seat or head; candidate requires selective terminal removal and retained housing integrity.
comparisons.reason: Insertion/latching and extraction/unlatching have different objectives and manipulation sequences.

comparisons.objective: Route a wire around posts and seat its final clip while preserving initial retention; candidate removes a terminal and wire from a connector cavity.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cable routing, bimanual span control, and clip insertion versus rigid tool insertion, tang release, and axial withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Wire follows the required route with both clips seated; candidate ends with the designated terminal extracted and neighboring terminals still seated.
comparisons.reason: Shared wire handling is incidental; the retention operation and endpoint are opposite.

comparisons.objective: Sort cubes while yielding safely to a person's hand; candidate performs connector rework.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed pick-place with human-avoidance constraints versus precision tool insertion and force-controlled bimanual extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Correctly sorted cubes without entering the shared bin during human occupancy; candidate requires selective depinning without component damage.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, skill, or success-condition overlap.

comparisons.objective: Align wire tips and twist a splice connector clockwise until snug; candidate extracts a crimp terminal from a housing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Wire-tip alignment and controlled helical fastening versus recessed blade insertion, tang depression, and axial pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Both wires captured at acceptable connector tightness without prohibited handling; candidate requires one intact wire-terminal assembly removed while the housing and neighbors remain sound.
comparisons.reason: Both concern wiring, but assembly by twisting is mechanically and functionally different from depinning.

comparisons.objective: Compress a loaded cell pack and insert a cross-key to retain preload; candidate releases retention to remove a terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Broad bimanual compression, plate alignment, and key insertion versus fine dual-blade release and opposite-side pull.
comparisons.success_condition: All cells remain compressed and retained by the seated key; candidate ends with retention defeated for exactly one terminal.
comparisons.reason: The tasks have opposite retention goals and substantially different contact mechanics.

comparisons.objective: Drive a piston through a ring compressor into a bore; candidate removes a retained connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a compressor flat while applying axial piston insertion force versus depress small tangs while pulling a wire-terminal assembly.
comparisons.success_condition: Piston seated without ring escape or jamming; candidate requires selective terminal exit without bypass, crimp failure, or collateral release.
comparisons.reason: Although both coordinate axial force with a second-hand constraint, their objectives and physical mechanisms differ.

comparisons.objective: Seat an ear probe, trigger measurement, hold it still, then place it down; candidate performs terminal extraction.
comparisons.physical_skill: Probe alignment, button press, and steady dwell versus extraction-tool insertion, retention release, and bimanual pulling.
comparisons.success_condition: Completed stable reading with safe probe handling; candidate requires physical removal of one retained terminal without damage.
comparisons.reason: No substantive overlap beyond precise insertion.

comparisons.objective: Lower a bent tube level so four legs seat simultaneously in a checking fixture; candidate extracts one connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual level transport and multi-point insertion versus fine tool alignment, tang depression, and opposed extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: All four tube legs seated and released at rest; candidate requires the selected terminal out and all other components retained.
comparisons.reason: Multi-point fixture seating is not retention release or depinning.

comparisons.objective: Release a cam-clamped camera plate, remove it, and place it on a pad; candidate releases tangs and removes a terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cam-lever actuation followed by payload lift-and-place versus sustained recessed dual-blade engagement during an axial wire pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Camera and plate clear the mount, remain attached, and rest upright on the pad; candidate requires selective terminal extraction with housing, wire, and neighbors intact.
comparisons.reason: Both release and remove a retained item, but the candidate's simultaneous internal release-and-pull mechanism and selective cavity constraints are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Immerse a wafer for a timed interval using pliers and return it to heater pins; candidate depins a connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool grasping, bath immersion, timer operation, and precise replacement versus tang-release tool insertion and coordinated extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct immersion duration and stable return without liquid-contact violations; candidate requires selective rearward terminal removal without damage.
comparisons.reason: No substantive overlap.

comparisons.objective: Join chain ends and slide a forked retaining plate under two pin heads; candidate removes a terminal by defeating retaining tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align multiple apertures and insert a slotted keeper sideways versus insert blades around one contact, depress tangs, and pull axially.
comparisons.success_condition: Chain joint assembled and positively retained; candidate ends with one component deliberately unretained and extracted.
comparisons.reason: The retention objectives are opposite and the insertion/extraction mechanics differ.

comparisons.objective: Close enclosure leaves in forced order and throw a bolt; candidate extracts a retained terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large articulated-door sequencing and bolt translation versus millimeter-scale tool guidance, force control, and opposed bimanual pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Both doors closed and bolted with hands clear; candidate requires one terminal removed while all other cavities remain retained.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective or physical-skill overlap.

comparisons.objective: Thread and hand-tighten an oil filter within a specified turn range; candidate removes a connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Axial thread engagement and controlled rotation versus blade-guided tang depression and linear extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Filter remains attached and neither loose nor overtightened; candidate requires complete selective removal without component damage.
comparisons.reason: Threaded installation and tang-released extraction are different manipulation constructs.

comparisons.objective: Insert opposed tapered shims until a door jamb is snug without bowing; candidate removes a retained terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual opposed wedge insertion and compliance judgment versus precision release-tool insertion and coordinated pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct shim overlap and snug jamb geometry without deformation; candidate requires terminal exit with reusable housing and retained neighbors.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual opposing actions do not produce the same objective or success state.

comparisons.objective: Recover a jammed drawer by compressing obstructing clothing before resuming opening; candidate releases an internal terminal retainer before extraction.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual obstruction compression and drawer pulling versus dual-blade tang depression and wire-terminal pulling.
comparisons.success_condition: Ordered jam, compression, clearance, and stable full opening; candidate requires selective terminal removal and explicit component-integrity constraints.
comparisons.reason: Both include release of resistance before pulling, but one is obstruction recovery and the other is a discrete retaining-feature extraction.

comparisons.objective: Transfer and count nuts using a tally counter; candidate performs selective connector depinning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated small-part pick-place and button actuation versus fine extraction-tool alignment and force-controlled bimanual withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Nut count and tally agree with all nuts transferred; candidate requires exactly one designated terminal extracted without collateral effects.
comparisons.reason: No substantive overlap.

comparisons.objective: Secure a housing in a rollover fixture, invert and lock it, then insert a pad; candidate removes a terminal from a fixed housing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential loading, bar closure, fixture rotation, bolt locking, and pad insertion versus internal tang release and wire pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct ordered fixture state with pad fitted and hands clear; candidate requires selective depinning with housing reuse.
comparisons.reason: The housing reference is superficial; objectives and mechanics are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Mount the final bicycle-tire bead section by creating slack in the rim channel; candidate extracts a terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Distributed compliant bead depression and rolling with two-hand coordination versus rigid precision tool insertion and tang release.
comparisons.success_condition: Bead fully mounted without tire lever or prohibited escape; candidate requires a designated terminal removed without damage or neighbor release.
comparisons.reason: The tire task is a validated deformable-style assembly operation, not rigid retention release.

comparisons.objective: Break an ampoule neck using a protective opener that captures the cap; candidate extracts a retained electrical terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Enclose, bend to break, and retain a separated cap versus align two blades, depress tangs, and maintain engagement during axial pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Confirmed break with cap contained, body upright, and tool returned; candidate requires intact selective terminal extraction and reusable housing.
comparisons.reason: Both use a specialized tool for separation, but the breakaway-and-capture mechanics and endpoint differ materially from reversible housing depinning.

comparisons.objective: Remove one chip from a packet while leaving the others inside; candidate removes one terminal while leaving neighboring terminals retained.
comparisons.physical_skill: Confined object grasp and withdrawal from a movable container versus guided tool insertion, spring-tang release, and bimanual wire pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one chip placed on a plate with packet and remaining chips undisturbed; candidate requires exactly the designated terminal extracted with housing, crimp, and neighbors undamaged.
comparisons.reason: The selective-removal success pattern is similar, but the candidate adds a necessary retention-release mechanism rather than mere confined retrieval.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate a tool tip by touching one reference point from four orientations; candidate uses a tool to release and extract a terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated point contact with angular diversity and stable holds versus constrained blade insertion, force-controlled tang depression, and coordinated pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Four distinct stable calibration poses at one point; candidate requires physical terminal exit with integrity and selectivity checks.
comparisons.reason: Precision tool-tip alignment is shared, but the objectives and resulting physical state are different.
